definitions.explanation: An imitation or simulation of something real, done for practice or testing purposes.

examples.japanese: {模擬|もぎ}{試験|しけん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{受|う}けた→受ける：01215_ukeru⟧。
{模擬|もぎ}⟦{裁判|さいばん}→裁判：02773_saiban⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{弁護士|べんごし}→弁護士：03150_bengoshi⟧⟦{役|やく}→役：12557_yaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{担当|たんとう}→担当：02567_tantou⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I played the role of lawyer in a mock trial.

examples.japanese: ⟦{文化祭|ぶんかさい}→文化祭：05589_bunkasai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{模擬|もぎ}{店|てん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧ことになった。
examples.english: We decided to set up a booth at the school festival.

notes:
Used as a prefix meaning mock, simulated, or practice. Almost always appears as the first element of a compound rather than standing alone.

COMPOUNDS:
- {模擬|もぎ}{試験|しけん} (⟦{模試|もし}→模試：11099_moshi⟧) — practice exam, mock test
- {模擬|もぎ}⟦{裁判|さいばん}→裁判：02773_saiban⟧ — mock trial
- {模擬|もぎ}{店|てん} — booth, stall (at a school festival)
- {模擬|もぎ}⟦{戦|せん}→〜戦：28346_sen⟧ — mock battle, war game
- {模擬|もぎ}⟦{面接|めんせつ}→面接：01100_mensetsu⟧ — mock interview

USAGE:
The abbreviated form ⟦{模試|もし}→模試：11099_moshi⟧ (from {模擬|もぎ}{試験|しけん}) is extremely common among students preparing for entrance exams. {模擬|もぎ}{店|てん} is a staple of Japanese school festivals (⟦{文化祭|ぶんかさい}→文化祭：05589_bunkasai⟧), where student groups run temporary food stalls and game booths.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦シミュレーション→シミュレーション：10960_shimyureeshon⟧ — simulation (loanword, often technical)
- ⟦{練習|れんしゅう}→練習：05323_renshuu⟧ — practice (general, not necessarily simulating something real)
